title: Remove Element
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer val, remove all occurrences of val in nums in-place. The relative order of the elements may be changed. The function should return the number of elements in nums which are not equal to val.
pseudocode:
function removeElement(nums, val):
  1. k = 0
  2. for i from 0 to length(nums) - 1:
  3.   if nums[i] != val:
  4.     nums[k] = nums[i]
  5.     k = k + 1
  6. return k

steps.note: Initialize 'k' to 0. This pointer will track the position where the next non-`val` element should be placed, and ultimately, be the count of non-`val` elements.
Start iterating through the array with pointer 'i' from the beginning.
Check if nums[i] (3) is not equal to val (3). It is equal, so we skip the assignment and effectively 'remove' it.
Increment 'i' and continue to the next element.
Check if nums[i] (2) is not equal to val (3). It is not equal.
Since nums[i] (2) is not val, assign nums[i] to nums[k]. This moves the valid element to the front of the array.
Increment 'k'. It now points to the next available slot for a non-val element, and also represents one valid element found.
Increment 'i' and continue to the next element.
Check if nums[i] (2) is not equal to val (3). It is not equal.
Assign nums[i] (2) to nums[k] (nums[1]). The element is already 2, so the array content appears unchanged.
Increment 'k'. Two valid elements have now been placed.
Increment 'i' and continue to the next element.
Check if nums[i] (3) is not equal to val (3). It is equal, so we skip the assignment.
Increment 'i'. The loop condition (i < length(nums)) is now false, so the loop terminates.
The loop has finished. Return 'k', which is the count of elements not equal to 'val'. The first 'k' elements of the array contain the desired result.
